claim.pdf_says: In the 7.3.17.2 LEAP-SECOND general format, '>>LEAP-SECOND' carries a full-width underline and 'OFF' carries an underline, but 'ON' is printed with NO underline. Verified by a 300 dpi crop of the brace: a rule sits under 'OFF' only.
claim.markdown_says: > **Figure notes (LEAP-SECOND directive syntax diagram).** `LEAP-SECOND`, `ON`, and `OFF` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). ... The braces enclose two alternatives, exactly one of which shall be selected.  [specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4547]
claim.why_it_matters: Same falsely-restrictive class as the FLAG-14 note: an underlined uppercase word is REQUIRED, a non-underlined one is OPTIONAL and may be omitted. Recording ON as required makes a bare '>>LEAP-SECOND' read as illegal, whereas the printed format permits selecting the ON alternative and omitting the optional word - which is exactly what 7.3.17.4 GR 2 and GR 4 ("When ON is specified or implied") presuppose. Implementing from this note would emit a diagnostic for legal source and would lose the implicit-ON case.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct pixel inspection of the 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v106/spec_p106.png, 2550x3300). I did not rely on the OCR text layer or on visual impression alone; I measured the ink. (1) Isolating the ON/OFF column (x=685..790) and profiling ink per row: 'ON' glyphs occupy rows 1236-1266, 'OFF' glyphs occupy rows 1295-1325, and 'OFF' carries a 3-px horizontal rule at rows 1338-1340. Between the bottom of ON (1266) and the top of OFF (1295) there are 28 consecutive rows (1267-1294) that are PURE WHITE - not merely below an ink threshold, but pixel minimum exactly 255 - re-checked at a deliberately loose threshold (<245) to catch any faint gray rule. There is none. (2) The null is well-controlled: the OFF rule sits 14 rows below the OFF glyph bottom, so an ON rule would fall at approximately rows 1279-1281; those rows are pure white. (3) A rasterizer-dropout explanation is excluded: the same figure renders two other rules at identical 3-px stroke weight - the LEAP-SECOND rule at rows 1300-1302 and the OFF rule at rows 1338-1340 - so the renderer plainly reproduces rules of this weight in this figure. (4) Horizontal run extraction confirms the rules are single continuous runs: row 1301 gives one run x=349..619 (under LEAP-SECOND) and row 1339 gives one run x=698..765 (68 px, exactly the width of OFF). So the printed figure underlines LEAP-SECOND and OFF, and prints ON bare. The markdown quote is accurate and verbatim: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4547 does assert '`LEAP-SECOND`, `ON`, and `OFF` are underlined in the printed standard (required words)'. This is not reflow, page-break furniture, hyphenation, or a formatting artifact - it is a false positive assertion about a normative typographic distinction. Two independent corroborations. First, INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: the same transcription already records ON as NOT underlined in every sibling ON/OFF directive figure note - FLAG-02 (line 4315, '`ALL` and `ON` are **not** underlined'), LISTING (4613, 'ON is **not** underlined in the printed figure'), PROPAGATE (4742, '`ON` is **not** underlined'), REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH (4837, '`ON` is printed **without** an underline'), and TURN (4912, 'Note that `ON` is printed **without** an underline, although `OFF` - its alternative in the same braces - is underlined'). Line 4547 and the FLAG-14 note at 4401 are the only two outliers, which is the signature of a transcription slip rather than a genuine ISO typesetting variation. Second, the semantic consequence the claim asserts is supported by the standard's own notation clause: 5.2 states that keywords are 'shown in uppercase and underlined ... They are required' (line 2628) and that optional words are 'shown in uppercase and not underlined ... may be written to add clarity' (line 2641), restated at line 5805 as 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.' Under that convention a bare '>>LEAP-SECOND' is legal and is equivalent to '>>LEAP-SECOND ON', which is precisely the implicit-ON route that 7.3.17.4 GR 2 and GR 4 ('When ON is specified or implied') require - GR 1 already accounts for implied OFF via directive absence, so ON must be implicable some other way. Implementing from the note as written would reject legal source. I found no basis to refute the claim on any of the rejection grounds.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two refinements to the claim's wording; neither weakens the finding. (a) The claim says "'>>LEAP-SECOND' carries a full-width underline". Measured precisely, the rule runs x=349..619 on rows 1300-1302, which begins at the 'L' of LEAP and ends at the 'D' of SECOND; the '>>' compiler-directive indicator (glyphs at x~295..337) is NOT underlined. So the underlined token is LEAP-SECOND alone, not '>>LEAP-SECOND'. This is immaterial to the defect and the markdown note does not misstate it. (b) The claim's interpretive leap - non-underlined ON is an OPTIONAL WORD, so '>>LEAP-SECOND' alone is legal and implies ON - is the reading sanctioned by 5.2 (lines 2628, 2641, 5805) and is the one I would adopt. Note however that the transcription itself floats a competing reading at line 4742 (PROPAGATE): 'In the compiler-directive formats the underlined alternative marks the default.' That alternative reading should be rejected, because it is falsified by LISTING: the LISTING note at line 4613 records OFF underlined and ON not, yet 7.3.18.3 GR 2 makes '>>LISTING ON' the DEFAULT - so 'underlined = default' cannot be right, while the optional-word reading explains LISTING, LEAP-SECOND, PROPAGATE, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH and TURN uniformly. THE FIX: at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 4547, change the note to read that LEAP-SECOND and OFF are underlined in the printed standard (required words) and that ON is printed WITHOUT an underline - an optional word per 5.2 - so that selecting the ON alternative and omitting the word yields a bare '>>LEAP-SECOND', which is the implicit-ON case presupposed by 7.3.17.4 GR 2 and GR 4. SCOPE: this is a pattern, not a one-off. The identically-worded FLAG-14 note at line 4401 makes the same false claim about ON and should be corrected in the same change set; the ISO_COBOL.md ON/OFF directive notes should then be swept as a group (FLAG-02 4315, FLAG-14 4401, LEAP-SECOND 4547, LISTING 4613, PROPAGATE 4742, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH 4837, TURN 4912) so all seven state the glyph facts and the optional-word consequence consistently. COMPILER IMPACT: the LEAP-SECOND directive parser must accept '>>LEAP-SECOND' with the ON phrase omitted and treat it as ON, and must not diagnose the bare form.
